games.name: SEND TO SPACE
games.character_role: Decal only. A ~14px character orb sits in a dark capsule inside the oval word badge that overlaps the rocket's nose (phone start/mid/finish tiles). The orb's colour changes per word (red, purple, blue), but it never reacts to the lever, never rides or waves from the rocket and never transforms. The ghost silhouettes in the backdrop are shared ambient decoration.
games.finale: Finish (phone and desktop finish tiles): the rocket is still on the pad, exactly where it started, with concentric rings and an empty 'STILL +1' toast. The promised launch that shrinks it to a pixel never happens. The reveal is the shared text card ('CALMER ✓ MORE SPACE AROUND IT'). Not unique.
games.score_rationale: A4: the chrome rocket has a gradient sheen, and the exhaust bloom (phone mid) is the only lit moment. Otherwise it is flat shapes on the shared nebula, with no launch pad, smoke, sky or planet. B4: the rocket prop is distinctive, but the backdrop is the shared nebula and the right-hand slider is the same control as 29 MUTE. C3: the lever is a cyan pill on a track with no notches or squash. The rocket does not move between the start, mid and finish tiles, so a pull has no visible result. D2: a tiny static orb in a word badge. E2: no launch; the shared reveal card. F5: 'Pull the lever' is clear, and on phone the lever now sits beside the rocket. But nothing shows which way to pull, and the word is about 10px. G5: the lever is a large thumb target, but the toast covers the guide line 'Pull the lever · 42% complete' (phone mid), plus header title clipped to 'MOTIONAL RELEASE CONSO' under the LVL pill and the input text running under the mic icon (all 390 tiles). H5: sending a worry into space fits worry and overwhelm, but without the shrink-to-a-pixel distance the player never feels the relief.
perf_flags: p95 750ms phone / 833ms desktop (over the 34ms limit; headless). Phone is about 1.7x the fleet median of 433ms.
Longest task 1023ms on desktop; 76 long tasks (11.6s total) on phone.
games.strengths: The rocket is a real object with a sheen, and the exhaust bloom at mid suggests ignition. On phone the lever sits beside the rocket, which partly fixes the catalog's complaint about a far-right lever. The metaphor is understood instantly.
games.problems: Phone start: the oval word badge overlaps the rocket body and the lever track. The character is a ~14px orb in a dark capsule (a black mask). Phone mid: the toast covers the guide text. Phone finish: the rocket sits where it started; nothing launched. Desktop: the rocket and lever are tiny in a mostly empty 1280 stage, and the labels are about 6px. The header title clipped to 'MOTIONAL RELEASE CONSO' under the LVL pill and the input text running under the mic icon (all 390 tiles). Both sizes use the shared reveal.
improvements: Make each pull a launch: the rocket crouches (10% squash) as the exhaust builds, lifts off with a smoke plume and a camera tilt, then shrinks to a star-sized pixel that twinkles out. A new rocket rolls onto the pad for the next round.
Put the emotion character in the cockpit window: anxious on the pad, squashed by g-force at lift-off, waving and smiling as it shrinks. The last rocket's character turns calm before it vanishes.
Unique finale: the six launched thoughts link up into a small new constellation that glows warm, while Earth rises in the foreground in sunrise light.
Build a launch-pad environment: a gantry, ground fog, Earth's horizon curve, warm sodium light from below and a parallax star field.

Make the lever a chunky throttle with notches, a click per notch, a knob that squashes and an arrow showing the pull direction. Raise the word to 15px or more and move it off the rocket body onto a hull or nose-cone label.
Dock the toast above the stage so it never covers the guide or the controls, and fix the clipped header title.

games.name: DROP ZONE

D1: no characters. E2: no payoff of its own; the shared reveal card. F4: 'Drop it' has no arrow, and the block reads as a card rather than a weight. The word is about 10px and 'WEIGHT' about 7px. Max frame 750ms on desktop.

games.problems: Phone start: a flat dark card with a ~10px word and a ~7px 'WEIGHT' tag; no drag arrow and no drop target below the ledge. Phone mid: the card jumps below the ledge with no fall, and the glow orb is detached from it. Phone finish: the card overlaps the top edge of the live guide panel, and the toast covers the 'Mind Bend' text. No characters anywhere. improvements: Make the weight heavy: a stone or iron block with the word carved into it at 15px or more. The drag should resist, the block should fall with acceleration, and the landing should squash it, shake the screen and puff dust.

Make a character the carrier: it starts stooped and straining under the block. With each drop it straightens, its shoulders lift and its face brightens, and after six drops it walks with a light bounce.
Unique finale: the dropped blocks sink into soft ground below the ledge and flowers sprout from them, while the now-light character floats up like a balloon into warm light.
Give the ledge a real setting: a cliff edge or dock above a canyon, with warm late-afternoon rim light and depth fog.
Add an arrow and a glowing drop zone below the ledge, keep the dropped card clear of the guide panel and dock toasts away from the guide.

Set it apart from 38 DRAWER: an archive room with tall shelves, labelled boxes and a warm desk lamp, where each archived thought gets a dated label so it reads as kept, not lost.
Make the characters archivists: a frazzled character holding a messy stack at the start files each card and wipes its brow, and by the end sits back calmly with a cup of tea.

games.name: MUTE
games.character_role: A decal that changes with each word, not with your actions. A ~18px character orb sits in a dark capsule in the word card: a blue face at phone start, a sleepy purple face at phone mid and a distressed red face for 'panic' at phone finish. It never reacts to the fader or quietens down, and it ends the game looking more upset, not calmer.
games.finale: Finish (phone finish tile): the waveform is a flat row of dots under a pale glow orb, with a 'STILL HIT · CHAIN ×6' toast. Desktop finish shows a tilted toast. The reveal is the shared text card. Not unique.
games.score_rationale: A5: the purple-blue waveform bars are the most vivid in-game graphic in the batch, and they collapse to a row of dots as you pull (phone start vs mid). But the glass panel, the white pill knob and the shared glow orb are flat. B4: a glass panel on the shared nebula, with no mixing desk, studio or radio. C5: the shrinking waveform is real live feedback, but the fader has no notches, click, knob squash or visible audio ducking. D3: a small decal whose face changes with the word and is distressed at the finish. E2: flat dots plus the shared reveal. F6: 'Turn it down', a fader and a loud waveform read within 2 seconds, but there is no arrow and the word is about 9px. G5: the fader track hangs below the glass panel and its knob overlaps the panel border (phone mid and finish), the toast covers the guide, and the header title clipped to 'MOTIONAL RELEASE CONSO' under the LVL pill and the input text running under the mic icon (all 390 tiles). H6: turning down the inner critic's volume is a strong metaphor for anxiety and overthinking, and watching the wave flatten supports it.
perf_flags: p95 433ms phone / 767ms desktop (over the absolute limits; headless). This is the fleet median.
games.strengths: The best feedback loop in the batch: the loud waveform visibly flattens as the fader comes down. The message ('quiet is enough; gone is optional') is clear and kind.
games.problems: Phone start, mid and finish: the ~18px character image sits in a dark capsule (a black mask), and the finish character is a distressed red face. The fader track extends outside the glass panel, and the knob overlaps the panel border (phone mid and finish). The toast covers the guide text (phone mid). The word is about 9px. The header title clipped to 'MOTIONAL RELEASE CONSO' under the LVL pill and the input text running under the mic icon (all 390 tiles). On desktop everything is small in the middle of an empty stage. Both sizes use the shared reveal.
improvements: Make the character the loud voice: a big shouting character with a megaphone whose mouth and body shrink as the fader drops. At low volume it yawns, whispers and curls up asleep with a soft 'zzz', a visible loud-to-calm change.
Build a radio or mixing-desk setting: a warm wooden console, a lit VU meter whose needle drops, glowing valves and soft studio light.
Make the fader tactile: a chunky knob with a click every 20%, slight resistance and overshoot, and audio that actually ducks in sync.
Unique finale: the ON AIR sign switches to OFF, the waveform settles into a slow breathing sine wave and the room dims to warm lamp light while the sleeping character snores softly.
Keep the track inside the panel, remove the dark capsule behind the character and raise the word to 15px or more.
